chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Surely, in this place, meaning when one passes the Yamani Corner, there is an Angel who has been granted the hearing of the people of the earth. So whoever sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he reaches it, the Angel delivers it to him.

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yamani Corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.سَمَاعَ أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ: Hearing of the people of the earth
key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the Yamani Corner during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual significance of the Yamani Corner (al-Rukn al-Yamani) as a conduit for divine acceptance, where an angel endowed with the ability to hear all earthly supplications conveys the pilgrim's blessings upon the Prophet directly to him. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the metaphysical reality of the Kaaba's corners as active nodes of spiritual connection, encouraging pilgrims to maximize their devotional acts during the circumambulation (Tawaaf). The emphasis on sending blessings (Salawat) at this specific moment reflects the belief in the immediate responsiveness of the Prophet to the faithful's devotion.
